changes: New Duplicate button on an item's page opens the Add Item form prefilled with that item's values, so similar items are added quickly; the copy is created only when you save it.
A duplicate never takes over the original's photos, container, or QR code, and a copied serial number carries a reminder that serial numbers are often unique.
New Templates page: save reusable presets for items you add often, with default values for every item field and the category's custom fields.

Use a template, or choose From template… in the Add item menu, to open the regular Add Item form prefilled; every value can be changed before the item is saved, and the item never stays linked to the template.
Save as template on an item's page starts a new template from that item, so item-specific values such as the serial number can be cleared first.
Templates are included in database backups and restores, and a template whose category or fields were deleted keeps working or asks to be repaired instead of failing.
The Dashboard now draws its metrics as charts: a photo coverage gauge, a placement bar, a daily chart of the last 30 days, a category treemap, and a condition donut, in both light and dark mode.
Click a category tile, or use the category buttons with the keyboard, to filter the Dashboard; every number is still shown as text too.
New Field coverage card shows how many items have photos, placement, condition, purchase date, purchase price, and serial number filled in, each on its own.
New Items by location card counts items by the location the Items list shows, so an item inside a box counts at the box's location.

Choose which item fields the Items list shows with the new Columns control, including purchase date and price, serial number, Transferred To, dates, and your own custom fields; Reset to default brings back the usual view.
Custom fields with the same name and type in different categories appear as one column, so a Brand column shows the brand of cameras and amplifiers alike.
Sort by clicking a column header, and click again to reverse; on a phone the cards show the chosen fields and a compact Sort control. The choice is remembered in this browser.
Search now also finds items by the values of text custom fields, whether or not their column is shown.

Error messages from the server now appear in the chosen interface language, English or Ukrainian, including refused deletions, invalid imports, backup and restore problems, cloud backup, AI provider, and update errors.
Counts in error messages use the right plural forms, and item, category, and field names inside them are shown exactly as you entered them.
Unexpected server failures now show a short generic message; their technical details stay in the server log instead of reaching the browser.
The interface is now available in English and Ukrainian: choose the language in Settings → Interface, and it changes at once without a reload.
The language is remembered in this browser only; English stays the default, and anything not yet translated falls back to English.
Dates, numbers, prices, and file sizes are shown in the format of the chosen language, while item names, categories, fields, and every other value you entered are never translated.
The Dropbox app key and secret and the Google Drive client ID and secret for Cloud Backup can now be entered in Settings instead of only as server environment variables.
The saved secret is never shown again: Settings displays only its last four characters, a blank field keeps it, and Remove deletes it once the provider is disconnected.
Added Cloud Backup to Settings: connect Dropbox or Google Drive and upload the same consistent database snapshot as Download backup with Backup now.
Automatic daily or weekly cloud backups run on the server at a time in its own time zone, can keep only the newest backups, and show their last result and next run.
Dropbox uses its own app folder and Google Drive only the Inventory Atlas Lite folder it creates; the stored access stays on the server and is never part of a backup.
AI features can now use OpenRouter, a local Ollama or LM Studio server, or any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint as well as OpenAI; choose the provider and its base URL in Settings.
Settings gained Test connection, a model list loaded from the chosen provider with text-only models marked, and an Image input option; existing OpenAI settings keep working unchanged.
A photo is never sent to a model known to be text-only, provider errors are explained in plain words, and the API key stays tied to the provider and address it was entered for.
Added Reset Inventory Database to a new Danger Zone on the Data / Backup page: it removes every item, photo, category, and custom field and leaves a fresh, empty database.
The dialog shows how much will be removed and needs a checkbox plus the typed phrase RESET INVENTORY; the server checks both and a single-use confirmation that expires after five minutes.
A verified safety backup is written to pre-reset-backups first and kept, a failed reset puts the previous inventory back automatically, and settings such as the AI key are not touched.
First published release with the Transferred To field from 0.28.0 and Batch Add from JSON from 0.29.0, whose releases were stopped by an unreliable automated test.
Fixed the timing of the label printing browser test; the application itself is unchanged.
Added Batch Add from JSON on the Items page: create up to 100 items of one category from a pasted JSON document.
Insert Template writes a document with every item attribute and the chosen category's custom fields.
Preview lets you edit or remove every proposed item and shows problems next to the affected value; the batch is created all at once or not at all.
Added a Transferred To field to every item for noting who or where it went when it was lent, given away, or sold.
The field suggests values already used on other items, and the item page and the Items list show a Transferred to badge while it is filled in.
Search on the Items page now also finds items by their Transferred To value.
Added QR label printing: tick items on the Items page, press Print Labels, and print their QR labels on A4 sheets or save them as PDF.
Choose a Large, Standard, or Compact layout and whether the name, description, category, and location appear next to the code.
The selection is kept across pages and filters, and the QR Code window can print a single item's label.
Added Scan QR: point the camera at an item label and the item opens.
When the camera is not available, for example over plain HTTP, a code can be read from a photo or screenshot with Scan from image.
Codes are decoded in the browser; camera frames and images are never uploaded, and only Inventory Atlas item codes are opened.
The update panel in About now shows the phases of an update, the exact step in progress, and the time elapsed.
Fixed an update that was stopped part-way, for example when the container ran out of memory, blocking every later update.
Background removal now frees its model memory after a few idle minutes.
New Proxmox installations get 2048 MiB of memory, enough to build an update while the application keeps running.
Added a QR code for every item, opened with the new QR Code button on the item page.
The code contains only the item's UUID, so a printed label keeps working after the installation moves or the database is restored elsewhere.
The code is generated locally in the browser and is never stored or uploaded.
Improved background removal: it is now about twice as fast and uses noticeably less memory, with the same cutout quality.
Improved background removal: a stronger local model produces a noticeably cleaner cutout of the item.
Improved background removal: leftover background fragments and translucent halos around the item are largely gone.
Added a subtle shadow under the item in the processed photo.
Note: background removal now takes a few seconds per photo, and installation downloads a larger model.
Added AI Add Item from a written description: a draft can now be created from a photo, a description, or both.
Improved AI Add Item: the photo is optional, the description is a first-class input, and the action is now called Create Draft.
Improved AI Add Item: background removal is offered only while a photo is selected and is never requested for a description-only draft.
Improved AI drafts: a disagreement between the description and the visible markings is reported as a warning for review.
Improved the Enable AI features setting: it now hides the AI Add Item and AI Add Fields actions while AI is turned off.
Improved direct navigation: the AI Add Item page returns to Items while AI features are disabled.
Improved Settings: saving a changed AI state applies to the interface immediately, without reloading the page.
Improved AI configuration: AI features can only be enabled once an OpenAI API key is saved, and removing the key turns them off.
Added Version History to the About dialog: a bundled timeline of releases and their user-visible changes.
Improved offline use: the release history is part of the application and needs no internet connection.
Added a field-definition template that can be inserted into the Batch Add Fields editor.
Added an update panel to the About dialog that checks for a newer stable release.
Added a confirmed self-update for Proxmox/LXC installations, with an automatic database backup and rollback.
Improved Docker installations: they report that the container must be updated from the Docker host.
Improved contained items: they are displayed at the location of their outermost container while their own saved location stays editable.
Maintenance release: the server was reorganized into route, service, and repository layers without changing any workflow.
Fixed the release check of the Docker image so published images are verified against the current health response.
Added a photo carousel to item details, with arrows, indicators, swipe, and drag.
Maintenance release: documented the backend architecture rules used for further development.
Added database restore from a downloaded backup, with server-side validation, a pre-restore safety backup, and automatic rollback.
Fixed backup handling so restore working directories are never picked up as repository content.
Added AI-generated field drafts: describe a category and review the proposed fields in the batch editor before creating them.
Added Batch Add Fields: paste a field-definition document, review and edit it, and create the fields in one batch.
Fixed the Docker image, which was missing the shared field-definition module.
Improved installation size and reliability by skipping the unused GPU inference providers.
Added an OpenAI model selector to the AI settings.
Maintenance release: stabilized the automated browser tests for AI background removal.
Added local AI background removal for item photos, which runs on the server without an external service.
Improved the quality of AI item identification from a photo.
Maintenance release: stabilized the automated browser test for the AI settings.
Added AI-assisted item creation: analyze a photo and review the editable draft before saving it.
Added the inventory dashboard with totals, documentation and placement metrics, and category and condition distributions.
Added an optional purchase date, a multi-currency price, and a serial number to every item.
Added the About dialog, which shows the version, the build revision, and the source date of the running build.
Added published releases: every stable tag now ships a Docker image and a verified source archive for Proxmox.
Fixed the stability of the automated browser tests.
Improved the whole interface by migrating it to the Tabler design system.
Fixed the light/dark toggle in the folded desktop sidebar.
Improved the interface on phones and tablets with a responsive redesign.
Added a Stored inside column to the items list.
Added the application title Inventory Atlas Lite to the interface.
Added a quick user guide to the repository documentation.
Fixed the Proxmox installer: it now picks the container template matching the host architecture and finds the container scripts.
Fixed the progress output of the Proxmox installer.
Fixed the download addresses used by the Proxmox installer.
Added nested items: an item can be stored inside another item and its direct contents can be browsed.
Added value suggestions for text custom fields.
Added the one-line Proxmox installer that creates a ready LXC container.
